content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
It uses the **gcloud CLI** (the easiest way) and also shows the equivalent **REST API** call so you can embed it in your own automation.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * Enable the Compute Engine API in your project.  
> * Install the Cloud SDK (`gcloud`) and authenticate (`gcloud auth login`).  
> * Make sure you have a GPU‑enabled zone (e.g. `us-central1-b`, `europe-west4-a`, etc.).  
> * Ensure the `nvidia-a6000` accelerator type is available in that zone.  

---

## 1. gcloud CLI command

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"          # GPU‑enabled zone
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk, 100 GB |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the GPU during maintenance |
| `--metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true` | Installs the NVIDIA driver automatically |
| `--tags` | Opens HTTP/HTTPS ports (optional) |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs, change `count=1` to the desired number (max 8 per instance in many zones).

---

## 2. REST API call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (e.g., from a script or CI/CD pipeline), here’s the exact payload you would POST to:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_OAUTH_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true" }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

Replace `{PROJECT}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual project ID and zone.  
Authenticate with an OAuth 2.0 token that has the `compute.instances.create` scope.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify the GPU is attached:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --format="get(guestAccelerators)"
```

You should see something like:

```
[
  {
    "acceleratorCount": 1,
    "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-b/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000"
  }
]
```

---

### Common pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **GPU type not available** | Check the zone’s GPU inventory: `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zone=$ZONE`. |
| **Instance fails to start** | Ensure the `install-nvidia-driver` metadata key is set; otherwise the driver won’t load. |
| **Billing error** | GPU instances incur extra charges; make sure billing is enabled for the project. |

---

That’s it! Run the gcloud command or POST the JSON payload, and you’ll have a fully‑functional Ubuntu 20.04 instance with an RTX A6000 GPU ready for your workloads.
